Cross-fitted exposure-only density ratios

Source: R/margot_lmtp_exposure_ratio.R
margot_lmtp_exposure_ratio.Rd

Estimate the ratio of the shifted exposure law to the natural exposure law by classifying equally weighted copies of each observed record. Each copy has the same history; its exposure is either observed or policy-shifted. Observation indicators and outcomes must be excluded from `history`. Both copies remain together in outer and inner validation, including the penalty-selection folds used by the default lasso learner.

Usage

margot_lmtp_exposure_ratio(
  data,
  exposure,
  history,
  shifted,
  id,
  fold_id,
  reached,
  learners = c("SL.mean", "SL.glmnet", "SL.ranger", "SL.xgboost"),
  inner_folds = 10L,
  structural_zero = rep(FALSE, nrow(data)),
  retain_fits = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the exposure and pre-exposure history.

exposure

Name of one numeric exposure column.

history

Unique names of pre-exposure predictors, excluding exposure.

shifted

Numeric vector of policy-shifted exposures in input row order.

id

Unique, nonmissing participant identifiers in input row order.

fold_id

Integer outer-fold assignments, numbered consecutively from one.

reached

Logical vector identifying records observed at this assignment.

learners

SuperLearner library, in order.

inner_folds

Number of participant-grouped inner validation folds. The default lasso learner retains ten separate penalty-selection folds.

structural_zero

Logical vector identifying observed exposure values outside the policy image. Defaults to no known structural zeros.

retain_fits

Logical. When `FALSE`, each outer fold's fitted SuperLearner is replaced, inside its worker, by a small record of learner names, ensemble coefficients, cross-validated risks, error flags and inner folds, so fitted learners never reach the calling process. Ratios, probabilities, validation membership and warnings are unchanged. Default `TRUE` keeps the earlier behaviour.

Value

A list containing uncapped `ratio`, classifier `probability`, complete outer-fold `fits`, input row identities and the requested learner settings. Unreached records have missing ratios and probabilities. Fits retain models, validation membership, warnings and worker process identifiers.

Details

No probability floor, ratio cap or observation probability is applied. A probability of one stops estimation unless a known structural zero is supplied for that evaluation record. The caller must justify structural zeros from the policy's image, rather than from fitted probabilities.

Configure the future plan, one thread per learner and the RNG before calling. The function uses `future.seed = TRUE`; it does not change the plan. Each outer fold is one future. It does not select an intervention schedule, estimate an outcome or establish adequate support.

References

Diaz et al. (2023), Nonparametric causal effects based on longitudinal modified treatment policies, Section 5.4.
